subproblem.title: Currents of degree exceeding the ambient dimension vanish
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with P < n, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set and let X ∈ D_n(U) (a GeometricCurrentOn U n). Then X(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U n), P < n → ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, X ω = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof (Case P < m + 1: any m+1 vectors of ℝ^P are linearly dependent, so every (m+1)-covector vanishes, every test form is 0, and X(ω) = X(0) = 0), written for a general degree n > P and domain U.

1. (Linear dependence.) Let x ∈ ℝ^P and v = (v_0, …, v_{n−1}) ∈ (ℝ^P)ⁿ. If v were linearly independent, then n = #Fin n ≤ dim ℝ^P = P (LinearIndependent.fintype_card_le_finrank, Fintype.card_fin, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), contradicting P < n. So v is linearly dependent.
2. (Vanishing covectors.) ω(x) is a continuous alternating n-linear map, and an alternating map vanishes on every linearly dependent family. Lean: AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent applied to the underlying alternating map (ω x).toAlternatingMap; this is applicable because ℝ is a field, so it is a domain and ℝ is torsion-free over itself. Hence ω(x)(v) = 0 for every v ∈ (ℝ^P)ⁿ, so ω(x) = 0 (ContinuousAlternatingMap.ext).
3. (Vanishing form.) Since x was arbitrary, ω = 0 as a function ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P). Hence ω = 0 as an element of the submodule Dⁿ(U) (Subtype.ext and funext).
4. (Conclusion.) X is linear (its underlying functional is a linear map), so X(ω) = X(0) = 0 (map_zero). ∎
proof_key_steps: Any n vectors in ℝ^P with P < n are linearly dependent (n = #Fin n ≤ finrank ℝ^P = P would fail).
Alternating maps vanish on linearly dependent families, so ω(x) = 0 for every x and ω = 0 in Dⁿ(U).

audit.reason: The proposition exactly states evaluation vanishing when P < n. The dimension bound forces every n-tuple to be linearly dependent; the alternating-map vanishing theorem applies over ℝ. Extensionality makes the test form zero, and current linearity finishes. This supplies the parent's lower-ambient-dimension case without additional assumptions.

subproblem.title: Mass inequality |Y(ω)| ≤ C·M(Y) under a pointwise bound |ω| ≤ C
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set, let Y ∈ D_n(U) (a GeometricCurrentOn U n) and ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) (a TestFormOn U n, i.e. a smooth compactly supported n-form on ℝ^P with tsupport ω ⊆ U), and let C ∈ ℝ with C > 0 and |ω(x)| ≤ C for every x ∈ ℝ^P, where |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} is Simon's Euclidean coefficient norm. Assume the mass M(Y) = Y.mass = M_U(Y) is finite. Then |Y(ω)| ≤ C·M(Y), where M(Y) ∈ [0, ∞) is read as a real number (ENNReal.toReal).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (Y : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (C : ℝ), 0 < C → (∀ x : Eucl P, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x) ≤ C) → Y.mass ≠ ∞ → |Y ω| ≤ C * Y.mass.toReal
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.4–2.5 (M(T) = sup over ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) with |ω| ≤ 1 of T(ω), the inner-product norm of Remark 2.6), and step 0 (Mass estimate) of the parent proof. Here the bound C > 0 plays the role of ‖ω‖ = sup|ω|.

Notation. |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α. By definition Y.mass = Y.massOn U is the supremum in [0, ∞] of ENNReal.ofReal(Y(η)) over η ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n U. That set consists of the η ∈ Dⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ U and |η(x)| ≤ 1 for all x ∈ ℝ^P. In particular (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn), every such η satisfies ENNReal.ofReal(Y(η)) ≤ Y.mass.

1. (Homogeneity of |·|.) For c ∈ ℝ and α ∈ Λⁿ(ℝ^P) we have |cα| = |c|·|α|.
  - For every strictly increasing I, (cα)(e_I) = c·α(e_I), so ((cα)(e_I))² = c²·α(e_I)². For I not strictly increasing, both summands are 0 = c²·0.
  - So the sum of squares for cα is c² times the sum s ≥ 0 for α: factor c² out of the finite sum.
  - Hence |cα| = √(c²·s) = √(c²)·√s = |c|·√s = |c|·|α|.
  (Lean: unfold covectorEuclideanNorm; use (c • α) v = c * α v, mul_pow, Finset.mul_sum, Real.sqrt_mul (sq_nonneg c) and Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs.)
  The library also gives |−α| = |α| (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
2. (Admissibility.) Let η ∈ Dⁿ(U) with |η(x)| ≤ C for all x ∈ ℝ^P, and put η′ := C⁻¹·η.
  - η′ ∈ Dⁿ(U), since Dⁿ(U) is a real submodule; hence tsupport η′ ⊆ U.
  - η′(x) = C⁻¹·η(x), so by step 1 and C⁻¹ > 0: |η′(x)| = C⁻¹·|η(x)| ≤ C⁻¹·C = 1 for every x.
  - So η′ ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n U, and ENNReal.ofReal(Y(η′)) ≤ Y.mass.
3. (One-sided bound.) Since Y.mass ≠ ∞, ENNReal.ofReal(a) ≤ Y.mass is equivalent to a ≤ (Y.mass).toReal (ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal). Y is linear, so Y(η′) = C⁻¹·Y(η). Hence C⁻¹·Y(η) ≤ (Y.mass).toReal. Multiplying by C > 0 gives Y(η) ≤ C·(Y.mass).toReal.
4. Apply steps 2–3 to η := ω, which satisfies |ω(x)| ≤ C by hypothesis: Y(ω) ≤ C·(Y.mass).toReal.
   Apply them to η := −ω, which satisfies |(−ω)(x)| = |−ω(x)| = |ω(x)| ≤ C by step 1: Y(−ω) = −Y(ω) ≤ C·(Y.mass).toReal.
5. Together, |Y(ω)| = max(Y(ω), −Y(ω)) ≤ C·(Y.mass).toReal. ∎
proof_key_steps: |cα| = |c|·|α| for the Euclidean coefficient norm (factor c² out of the sum of squares, √(c²s) = |c|√s).
If |η| ≤ C pointwise then C⁻¹η is mass-admissible, so ENNReal.ofReal(C⁻¹·Y(η)) ≤ M(Y).
Because M(Y) ≠ ∞ this gives Y(η) ≤ C·M(Y).toReal.
Apply to η = ω and η = −ω to obtain |Y(ω)| ≤ C·M(Y).toReal.

audit.reason: The proposition exactly matches the stated positive pointwise bound and finite mass assumption. The proof establishes homogeneity of the actual coefficient norm, preserves test-form support under scaling, derives the one-sided estimate using finite-mass toReal conversion, and applies it to both signs. It works for arbitrary U and contains no circular reliance.

subproblem.title: Test forms have bounded Euclidean coefficient norm
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set and let ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) (a TestFormOn U n: a smooth, compactly supported n-form on ℝ^P with tsupport ω ⊆ U). Then there is C ∈ ℝ with C > 0 such that |ω(x)| ≤ C for every x ∈ ℝ^P, where |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2}.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (ω : TestFormOn U n), ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ x : Eucl P, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x) ≤ C
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the Notation paragraph of the parent proof (‖ω‖ := sup_x|ω(x)| is finite for test forms because they are continuous with compact support). Here that finiteness is proved in the form of an explicit positive bound.

1. (|·| is continuous on Λⁿ(ℝ^P).)
  - For each fixed v ∈ (ℝ^P)ⁿ, the evaluation α ↦ α(v) is continuous on the space of continuous alternating maps (continuous_eval_const; the instance is ContinuousAlternatingMap.instContinuousEvalConst).
  - Hence, for each I : Fin n → Fin P, the map α ↦ (if I is strictly increasing then α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})² else 0) is continuous: it is either the square of a continuous function or the constant 0.
  - The finite sum over I is continuous (continuous_finsetSum), and composing with the continuous square root (Real.continuous_sqrt) shows that α ↦ |α| is continuous.
2. (Continuity of f.) ω is smooth (ContDiff ℝ ∞; this is the first component of the test-form property of ω), hence continuous. So f(x) := |ω(x)| is continuous on ℝ^P, as a composition of continuous maps.
3. (Compact support of f.) If ω(x) = 0 then f(x) = |0| = 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero). Hence support f ⊆ support ω ⊆ tsupport ω. Since ω has compact support, f has compact support (HasCompactSupport.mono'). (Lean remark: in this environment use mono' here; HasCompactSupport.comp_left produced a whnf heartbeat timeout in a scratch check, while mono' compiled.)
4. (Boundedness.) A continuous, compactly supported real function is bounded (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support): there is C₀ ∈ ℝ with |f(x)| ≤ C₀ for all x ∈ ℝ^P. In particular C₀ ≥ |f(0)| ≥ 0.
5. Put C := C₀ + 1. Then C ≥ 1 > 0, and for every x, f(x) ≤ |f(x)| ≤ C₀ < C. ∎
proof_key_steps: α ↦ |α| is continuous: evaluations of continuous alternating maps are continuous, then a finite sum of squares and a square root.
x ↦ |ω(x)| is continuous and has compact support, because ω is smooth with compact support and |0| = 0.
A continuous compactly supported real function is bounded by some C₀ ≥ 0; take C := C₀ + 1 > 0.

audit.reason: The proposition matches all stated quantifiers and hypotheses. Continuous alternating-map evaluation gives continuity of the finite sum of squares and its square root. The support inclusion gives compact support; boundedness followed by C₀ + 1 supplies the required positive global bound. The relevant instances and proof steps were independently checked.

subproblem.title: Decompositions X − P_k = ∂R_k + S_k with vanishing masses imply weak convergence
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set and let X ∈ D_{m+1}(U). For k ∈ ℕ let P_k, S_k ∈ D_{m+1}(U) and R_k ∈ D_{m+2}(U) (GeometricCurrentOn) satisfy X(ω) − P_k(ω) = ∂R_k(ω) + S_k(ω) for every k and every ω ∈ D^{m+1}(U), where ∂R_k(ω) = R_k(dω). Suppose M(R_k) → 0 and M(S_k) → 0 in [0, ∞] as k → ∞, where M = mass = M_U. Then P_k ⇀ X, i.e. P_k(ω) → X(ω) for every ω ∈ D^{m+1}(U) (WeaklyConvergesOn P_k X).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (Pk S : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (R : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 2)), (∀ (k : ℕ) (ω : TestFormOn U (m + 1)), X ω - Pk k ω = (R k).boundary ω + S k ω) → Tendsto (fun k => (R k).mass) atTop (𝓝 0) → Tendsto (fun k => (S k).mass) atTop (𝓝 0) → WeaklyConvergesOn Pk X
subproblem.natural_proof:
Sources:
- The printed proof of Simon 6.2: (1) T − P_k = ∂R_k + S_k; (2) M(R_k) ≤ cρ_kM(T) → 0 and M(S_k) ≤ cρ_kM(∂T) → 0; and 'Evidently (1), (2) give P_k(ω) → T(ω)'.
- Step 3(a) of the parent proof.
- The sibling lemmas mass_estimate (the estimate of step 0) and testform_bounded (finiteness of sup|ω|).

Notation: M = mass, |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α.

1. Fix ω ∈ D^{m+1}(U) and put dω := exteriorDerivativeTestOn U (m+1) ω ∈ D^{m+2}(U). By the definition of the boundary (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply), ∂R_k(ω) = R_k(dω) for every k.
2. By testform_bounded, choose C₁ > 0 with |ω(x)| ≤ C₁ for all x ∈ ℝ^P, and C₂ > 0 with |dω(x)| ≤ C₂ for all x ∈ ℝ^P.
3. (Finiteness and real limits.)
  - Since M(R_k) → 0 and 0 ≠ ∞, the neighbourhood {a ∈ [0, ∞] : a ≠ ∞} of 0 eventually contains M(R_k) (eventually_ne_nhds). So there is k₀ with M(R_k) ≠ ∞ for all k ≥ k₀. Likewise there is k₁ with M(S_k) ≠ ∞ for all k ≥ k₁.
  - ENNReal.toReal is continuous at 0 ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.tendsto_toReal), so M(R_k).toReal → 0 and M(S_k).toReal → 0 in ℝ.
4. (Estimate.) Let k ≥ max(k₀, k₁). Apply mass_estimate to Y = R_k, the form dω and C = C₂ (M(R_k) ≠ ∞), and to Y = S_k, the form ω and C = C₁ (M(S_k) ≠ ∞). Together with the hypothesis this gives
   |X(ω) − P_k(ω)| = |R_k(dω) + S_k(ω)| ≤ |R_k(dω)| + |S_k(ω)| ≤ C₂·M(R_k).toReal + C₁·M(S_k).toReal.
5. (Squeeze.) By step 3 the right-hand side tends to C₂·0 + C₁·0 = 0. Since the bound holds for all large k, the squeeze theorem (squeeze_zero_norm') gives X(ω) − P_k(ω) → 0.
6. Hence P_k(ω) = X(ω) − (X(ω) − P_k(ω)) → X(ω) − 0 = X(ω). Since ω ∈ D^{m+1}(U) was arbitrary, P_k ⇀ X. ∎
proof_key_steps: Fix ω; ∂R_k(ω) = R_k(dω) with dω = exteriorDerivativeTestOn U (m+1) ω ∈ D^{m+2}(U).
M(R_k), M(S_k) are eventually finite and their real values tend to 0.
|X(ω) − P_k(ω)| ≤ C₂·M(R_k) + C₁·M(S_k) → 0 by mass_estimate; hence P_k(ω) → X(ω).

audit.reason: The exact degrees, decomposition identity, ENNReal limits, and weak-convergence conclusion match the prose. Exterior differentiation preserves the required test-form space. Convergence to zero gives eventual finiteness and convergence of real masses; the two declared dependencies then provide the eventual estimate and squeeze argument. These dependencies are sufficient and non-circular.
